spans.s:
शल् शल् [cf. rt. चल्], cl. 1. A. शलते,
शेले, शलितुम्, to shake, tremble; to
cover; cl. 1. P. शलति, शशाल, &c., to go, move,
flow, run [cf. उच्-छल्, प्रोच्-छल्, rts. श्वल्, 3. शठ्];
cl. 10. A. शालयते, -यितुम्, to praise, (in this
sense also written शठ्.)

शल्ल् शल्ल्, a Sautra root meaning ‘to
go.’

शाल् शाल् [cf. rt. शाड्], cl. 1. A. शालते,
शालितुम्, to flatter, praise, coax; to
boast; to shine or be endowed with [see Malli-
nātha's commentary to Kirāt.

सल् सल् (connected with rt. सृ), cl. 1.
P. सलति, ससाल, सलितुम्, to go, move;
[cf. Gr. ἅλλ-ο-μαι, ἅλμα; Lat. salio; Lith. selu,
‘to creep;’ Slav. sl-a-ti, ‘to send;’ Hib. silim, ‘I
drop, distil, spit.’]

शल, अस्, अम्, m. n. (said to be fr. rt. शल्, but
probably connected with rt. शॄ), the quill of a por-
cupine; (अस्), m. a dart, spear; a stake; a kind of
field; N. of Bhṛṅgi (one of Śiva's attendants); of
Brahmā; of a son of Soma-datta; of a son of Dhṛta-
rāṣṭra; (ई), f. a small porcupine or hedgehog.

शल्ल, अस्, m. a frog; (अम्), n. bark, rind; [cf.
शल्क.]

शाल शाल, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. शल् or
rt. शाल् or rt. शो; in some senses also written साल,
q. v.), a particular tree, the Shorea Robusta or Valeria
Robusta (said to be one of the most valuable Indian
timber trees, = सर्ज, cf. साल); a tree (in general);
an enclosure, court, fence (= प्राकार); a kind of
fish, Ophiocephalus Wrahl; N. of a river; of king
Śāli-vāhana; (आ), f. a large branch, the upper or
main branch of a tree; a hall, saloon, large room,
apartment, room; a house; a stable; [cf. Angl. Sax.
heal, ‘a hall;’ Mod. Germ. Saal, Halle.]
—शाल-
ग्राम, अस्, m., N. of a sacred place or district; a par-
ticular sacred stone worshipped by the Vaiṣṇavas, (it
is said to be a kind of black ammonite, and its various
circular formations are supposed to have a mystical
significance and to be typical of Viṣṇu; these stones
are chiefly found in or near the river Gaṇḍakī, and
the circles or spirals they contain are thought by
some to be formed by the Vajra-kīṭa or other in-
sects; cf. साल-ग्राम.)
—शालग्राम-गिरि, इस्, m.,
N. of a mountain producing the Śāla-grāma.
—शा-
लग्राम-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha.
—शाल-
ग्राम-शिला, f. the Śāla-grāma stone.
—शाल-ज,
अस्, m. a kind of fish, (see above.)
—शाल-निर्यास,
अस्, m. resin, the resinous exudation of the Śāl tree
or Shorea Robusta.
—शाल-पर्णी, f. ‘having Śāl
leaves,’ the shrub Hedysarum Gangeticum, (also
written साल-पर्णी.)
—शाल-पोत, अस्, m. a young
Śāl tree.
—शाल-भञ्जिका, f. a doll, wooden puppet;
a courtezan, harlot; a kind of game played in the
east of India; [cf. साल-भञ्जिका.]
—शालभञ्-
जिका-प्रख्य, अस्, आ, अम्, resembling the game
called Śāla-bhañjikā.
—शाल-भञ्जी, f. a doll, wooden
puppet (as made of Śāl wood).
—शाल-वेष्ट, अस्,
m. the resin of the Śāl tree (used as incense &c.),
resin (in general).
—शाल-सार, अस्, m. a tree;
Asa Fetida, (also written साल-सार.)
—शालाङ्की
(˚ला-अङ्˚?), f. a doll, puppet.
—शालाजिर (˚ला-अज्˚?),
अस्, अम्, m. n. a hollow earthen cup or saucer.
—शाला-द्वार, अम्, n. the door or entrance of a
hall.
—शालाद्वार्य, अस्, m., scil. अग्नि, a kind of
sacred or sacrificial fire.
—शाला-मृग, अस्, m. ‘house-
animal,’ a jackal (as prowling near houses?).
—शाला-
वती, f., N. of one of the wives of Viśvā-mitra and
mother of Hiraṇyākṣa.
—शालावत्य, आस्, m. pl., N.
of a family descended from Viśvā-mitra.
—शाला-वृक,
अस्, m. ‘house-wolf,’ a dog; a cat; a jackal; a wolf; a
deer; a monkey; a particular class of evil or malicious
beings, (Mahā-bhārata, Śānti-parvan 1188.)
—शाला-
वृकेय, अस्, m. the offering of a Śālā-vṛka.
सल, अम्, n. [cf. सर], water.

साल साल, अस्, m. (= शाल, q. v.), the Śāl
tree or its resin; any tree; a fence or wall surround-
ing a building; any wall; a kind of fish, Ophio-
cephalus Wrahl; (आ), f. a house (more usually written
शाला).
—साल-ग्राम, अस्, m., N. of a sacred place;
the Śāla-grāma stone, (see शाल-ग्राम.)
—साल-
ग्राम-क्षेत्र, अम्, n., N. of a district.
—साल-
ज्य, अम्, n., N. of a place.
—साल-निर्यास, see
शाल-निर्यास.
—साल-पर्णी, see शाल-पर्णी.
—साल-पुष्प, अम्, n. a flower of the Sāl tree;
the shrub Hibiscus Mutabilis.
—साल-भञ्जिका, see
शाल-भञ्जिका.
—साल-रस, अस्, m. the resin of
the Sāl or Śāl tree.
—साल-वाहन, incorrect for
शालि-वाहन.
—साल-वेष्ट, see शाल-वेष्ट.
—सा-
ल-शृङ्ग, अम्, n. ‘wall-pinnacle,’ the coping of a
wall.
—साल-सार, see शाल-सार.
—साला-करी, f.
(according to some) ‘house-worker,’ a female cap-
tive (especially one won in battle).
—साला-वृक, अस्,
m. (see शाला-वृक), a dog; a jackal; a hyena; a
wolf; a wolf-like or cruel man.
शलक, अस्, m. a spider.

शलाका, f. a javelin, dart; an arrow; a rib (of an
umbrella &c.); a thin bar (as of a cage &c.), any
small stake, stick, rod, peg, pin; a round pointed
piece of wood or bamboo serving for various pur-
poses; a ruler; a brimstone match; any pointed
surgical instrument, a tent or probe (used in the
[]
treatment of external organic affections and some-
times taken as the N. of this branch of surgery; cf.
शालाक्य); a bone; an oblong quadrangular piece
of ivory or bone (used in playing a particular game),
a domino; a fibrous stick used as a brush, &c.; a
tooth-brush; a tooth-pick; a pencil; a sprout, sprig,
shoot of any kind [cf. रत्न-शलाका]; a porcupine;
a particular thorny shrub, Vangueria Spinosa; the
Sārikā bird, Turdus Salica.
—शलाक-धूर्त, अस्,
m. (for शलाका-ध्˚), cheating with dominoes, a
sharper.
—शलाका-परि, ind. an unlucky throw or
movement of one of the pieces at the game of
Śalākā, (see परि.)
—शलाका-पुरुष, आस्, m. pl.,
N. of sixty-three divine personages according to the
Jainas (viz. the twenty-four Jainas, twelve Cakra-
vartins, nine Vāsudevas, nine Bala-devas, and nine
Prati-vāsudevas).
शलाका शलाका. See p. 995, col. 3.

शल्लक, अस्, m. the plant Bignonia Indica, =
शोण; (अम्), n. bark, rind; (ई), f. a porcupine;
the gum olibanum tree, Boswellia Thurifera (=
गज-भक्षा, सुरभि).
—शल्लकी-द्रव, अस्, m.
‘Śallakī-essence,’ incense, olibanum (= सिह्ल).

शालक, अस्, m., N. of a man (perhaps a jester in
a play).

शालाक शालाक (fr. शलाका), Ved. a frag-
ment or splinter of wood, a chip.
शलल, अम्, n. the quill of a porcupine.

शलली, f. the quill of a porcupine; a small porcu-
pine.

शल्य, अस्, अम्, m. n. a dart, javelin, spear tipped
with iron, (उप-शल्य, a short spear); a pike; an
arrow, shaft; any stake or rod, spike, splinter, thorn,
(in these senses usually अम्, n.); a pin, peg; (अस्),
m. a porcupine, hedgehog; extraction of splinters
or extraneous substances in surgery (as a branch of
medicine or Āyur-veda, q. v.); the thorny shrub,
Vangueria Spinosa (= मदन); another tree (=
विल्व); a fence, boundary; a kind of fish; N. of
the king of Madra (maternal uncle of the sons of
Pāṇḍu and especially of Nakula and Sahadeva, Madrī
the wife of Pāṇḍu being sister to Śalya); (अम्), n.,
N. of a son of Vipracitti; (अम्), n. an iron crow-
bar; any extraneous substance lodged in the body
(as an arrow, thorn, splinter); a bone; sin, crime;
poison; difficulty, embarrassment, distress; abuse,
defamation; [cf. Gr. κῆλα; Hib. cail, ‘a spear.’]
—शल्य-कण्ठ, अस्, m. ‘quill-throated,’ a porcu-
pine.
—शल्य-क्रिया, f. the extraction of thorns or
other extraneous substances lodged in the body.
—शल्य-तन्त्र, अम्, n., N. of a section of the
Aṣṭāṅga-hṛdaya-saṃhitā (comprising chapters 25 —
34 of the Uttara-tantra or sixth book, and treating
of the cure of external wounds).
—शल्य-पर्वन्,
अ, n., N. of the ninth book of the Mahā-bhārata,
(this book describes how, on the death of Karṇa,
Śalya, king of Madra, was appointed to the command
of the Kuru army, and how a combat with maces
took place between Śalya and Bhīma, and another
great battle between Śalya and Yudhi-ṣṭhira, in
which the former was eventually killed.)
—शल्य-
प्रोत, अस्, आ, अम्, pierced or transfixed by an arrow.
—शल्य-लोमन्, अ, n. a porcupine's quill.
—शल्य-
वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, possessing an arrow, owning shafts;
shooting arrows, one who has shot an arrow; set
with stakes, hampered or harassed with difficulties.
—शल्य-वारङ्ग, अम्, n. ‘arrow-handle,’ the part
by which an arrow or other foreign substance lodged
in the body is laid hold of during the operation of
extraction.
—शल्य-शास्त्र, अम्, n. ‘splinter-(extrac-
tion)-science,’ that part of surgery which treats of
the removal of extraneous substances lodged in the
body; [cf. आयुर्-वेद.]
—शल्य-हर्तृ, ता, m. a
remover of thorns, weeder.
—शल्यारि (˚य-अरि), इस्,
m. ‘enemy of Śalya,’ an epithet of Yudhi-ṣṭhira.
—शल्याहरण-विधि (˚य-आह्˚), इस्, m. ‘method
of extracting splinters or other foreign substances,’
N. of the twenty-eighth chapter of the Sūtra-sthāna
or first book of the Aṣṭāṅga-hṛdaya-saṃhita.
—श-
ल्योद्धार (˚य-उद्˚), अस्, m. extraction of arrows or
thorns or other pointed substances from the body;
weeding; the ceremony of cleansing or purifying a
new house.
शल्य शल्य, &c. See col. 1.

शल्यक, अस्, m. a dart, javelin, spear, pike; a
stake, thorn; a porcupine; a hedgehog; the thorny
shrub Vangueria Spinosa.

शलङ्ग शलङ्ग, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt.
शल्), a king, sovereign (= लोक-पाल), a kind of
salt.

सालङ्ग सालङ्ग, अस्, m. a kind of Rāga or
musical mode.

शलभ शलभ, अस्, m. (according to Uṇā-
di-s.
III. 122

. fr. rt. शल्, but cf. शरभ), a grass-
hopper; a locust; a moth; N. of an Asura.
—श-
लभ-त्व, अम्, n. the state or condition of a grass-
[]
hopper.
—शलभासुर (˚भ-अस्˚), अस्, m. the
Asura Śalabha.

शलाट शलाट, अस्, m. (etymology doubt-
ful), a cartload (= 20 times 100 Palas).

शलाटु शलाटु, उस्, उस्, उ (said to be fr. rt.
शल्), unripe (as fruit); (उस्), m. a kind of root.

शलातुर शलातुर, N. of the abode of the
ancestors of Pāṇini; [cf. शालातुरीय.]

शलाभोलि शलाभोलि, इस्, m. (etymology
doubtful), a camel.

शलालु शलालु, n. a sort of perfume or
fragrant substance.

शलालुक, अस्, ई, अम्, purchased with or exchanged
for the substance termed Śalālu; [cf. शालालुक.]

शालालुक शालालुक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शलालु),
purchased with the perfume called Śalālu.

सललूक सललूक, अस्, m. (probably fr. rt.
सल्; according to Sāy. for सररूक, fr. rt. सृ),
Ved. (probably) an unstable or wavering person;
a wicked person, sinner, (Sāy. = सरण-शील or
संलुब्ध or पापक; see Nirukta
VI. 3
शल्क शल्क, अम्, n. (according to Uṇādi-s.
III. 43

. fr. rt. शल्, but probably connected with शल
and rt. शॄ), a part, portion, piece; bark (of a tree),
rind; the scale of a fish; [cf. वल्क.]
—शल्क-
मय, अस्, ई, अम्, scaly, flaky.

शल्कल, अम्, n. a part, portion; bark, rind; the
scale of a fish.
शल्कलिन्, ई, m. ‘having scales,’ a fish.
शल्किन्, ई, m. ‘having scales,’ a fish.

शल्पदा शल्पदा, f., N. of a plant or root
(= मेदा).
शल्पपर्णिका शल्प-पर्णिका = शल्पदा.

शल्भ् शल्भ्, cl. 1. A. शल्भते, शशल्भे,
शल्भितुम्, to praise; to boast.

शल्मलि शल्मलि, इस्, m. the silk-cotton
tree; [cf. शाल्मलि.]
शल्मली, f. = शल्मलि above.

शाल्मलि, इस्, m. f. the Seemul or silk-cotton tree,
Bombax Heptaphyllum, (कूट-शाल्मलि, a fabulous
thorny rod of the cotton tree for torturing the wicked
in hell); one of the seven Dvīpas or great divisions
of the known continent (so called from the above
tree said to grow there; it is surrounded by the sea
of ghee or clarified butter); a kind of hell in which
the wicked are tormented with the thorns or prickles
of the Śālmali.
—शाल्मलि-द्वीप, अस्, m. the Śāl-
mali-dvīpa.
—शाल्मलि-पत्त्रक, अस्, m. the Sapta-
cchada tree.
—शाल्मलि-स्थ, अस्, m. ‘Śālmali-abid-
ing,’ epithet of Garuḍa.

शाल्मली, f. = शाल्मलि above; N. of a river in the
infernal regions (Manu
IV. 90

); of a hell, (see शाल्-
मलि); of one of the Śaktis of Viṣṇu.
—शाल्मली-
कन्द, अस्, m. the root of the Śālmali tree.
—शाल्-
मली-फल, अस्, m. a particular plant or tree (=
तेजः-फल).
—शाल्मली-फलक, अम्, n. a smooth
board of Śālmalī wood (used to wash clothes upon).
—शाल्मली-वेष्ट or शाल्मली-वेष्टक, अस्, m. the
gum or resin of the silk-cotton tree.

शल्व शल्व, अस्, m., N. of a country, (more
usually written शाल्व, q. v.)

शाल्व शाल्व, अस्, m., N. of a country, (also
written साल्व, q. v.); a king of the Śālvas; (आस्),
m. pl., N. of a tribe (inhabiting Bhārata-varṣa).
—शाल्व-पति, इस्, or शाल्व-राज, अस्, or शाल्व-
राजन्, आ, m. the king of the Śālvas.

सल्व सल्व, आस्, m. pl., Ved., N. of a peo-
ple; [cf. शल्व.]
—सल्व-देश, अस्, m., N. of a
country.

साल्व साल्व, अस्, m., N. of a demon-king
who was slain by Viṣṇu, (according to the Śabda-k.
he was king of the country of Saubha); N. of a
country (more usually written शाल्व); (आस्), m. pl.
the inhabitants of Sālva; (अस्, ई, अम्), belonging to
the country Sālva.
—साल्व-हन्, आ, m. ‘slayer of
Sālva,’ N. of Viṣṇu.
शालाक्ष, आस्, m. pl., N. of a family or Gotra.

सलक्ष स-लक्ष, अस्, आ, अम्, having a lac
or a hundred thousand.
शालानी, f. the shrub Hedysarum Gangeticum.

शालार, अम्, n. a ladder, flight of stairs or steps;
a bird-cage; the claw of an elephant.

सालार, अम्, n. a pin or peg projecting from a
wall, a bracket, shelf.

शालिक, अस्, ई, अम्, relating or belonging to the
Śāl tree; belonging to a hall, &c.; (अस्), m. a
weaver; a village of artificers; a toll, tax; (आ), f. the
shrub Hedysarum Gangeticum; N. of a Mīmāṃsā
work by Śālikā-nātha (= प्रकरण-पञ्चिका).
—शालिका-नाथ, अस्, m., N. of the author of the
Śālikā and of the Praśasta-pāda-bhāṣya-vyākhyāna
commentary.
शालिक शालिक. See under शाल, p. 1002.

शालिन्, ई, इनी, इ, belonging to a house, domestic,
&c.; endowed with, possessed of, possessing, having;
shining or resplendent with (generally at the end of
comps., cf. वीर्य-श्˚; in this sense apparently con-
nected with rt. शाल्); (इनी), f. a mistress of a house,
housekeeper; a kind of metre, four times ¯¯¯¯¯
˘¯¯˘¯¯; a proper N.
—१. शालि-ता, f. or शालि-
[]
त्व, अम्, n. the being endowed with, possession;
confidence in.

शालिन, अस्, आ, अम्, for शालीन below.
—शालिनी-
करण, see शालीनी-करण.

शालीन, अस्, आ, अम्, attached to the house or to
one's own room, domestic, bashful, humble, retiring,
ashamed; like, resembling; (अस्), m. a householder,
one who devotes himself to household or worldly af-
fairs; (आ), f. a sort of fennel (= मिश्रेया).
—शालीन-
ता, f. or शालीन-त्व, अम्, n. bashfulness, modesty.
—शा-
लीनत्व-विवर्जित, अस्, आ, अम्, devoid of modesty,
immodest.
—शालीन-शील, अस्, आ, अम्, of a bashful dis-
position or retiring nature.
—शालीनशील-ता, f. bash-
fulness.
—शालीनी-करण, अम्, n. the making hum-
ble, humbling; abuse, reproach.
—शालीनी-कृ, cl. 8.
P. -करोति, &c., to make humble, humiliate.
शालीन शालीन. See p. 1002, col. 3.
शाली, f. a kind of plant (= कृष्ण-जीरक).

शालि शालि, इस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. शाल् or
fr. rt. शॄ, cf. Uṇādi-s.

), rice (of which there
are said to be ten varieties; but especially two kinds,
one white, growing in deep water, and the other red,
requiring only a moist soil); the civet-cat, pole-cat;
N. of a Yakṣa transformed into a lion, (see शालि-
वाहन); (अयस्), m. pl. grains of rice, rice.
—शालि-
कण, अम्, n. a grain of rice.
—शालि-चूर्ण, अस्,
अम्, m. n. rice-flower, ground rice.
—२. शालि-ता, f.
or शालि-त्व, अम्, n. the state or condition of rice.
—शालि-पर्णी, f. a kind of leguminous shrub (=
माष-पर्णी).
—शालि-पिष्ट, अम्, n. ‘flour of
rice,’ crystal.
—शालि-भवन, अम्, n. a rice field.
—शालि-वाह्, वाट्, -ल्यूही, वाट्, see Vopa-deva

IV.

.
—शालि-वाह, अस्, m. a proper N.
—शालि-वा-
हन, अस्, m., N. of a celebrated sovereign of India
(said to be so called either from having in his infancy
ridden on a Yakṣa called Śāli, or from Śāli for Śāla,
the Śāl tree, Śāli-vāhana being represented as borne
on a cross made of that or other wood; he was the
enemy of Vikramāditya and institutor of the era
now called Śāka, commencing from his birth, seventy-
eight years after Christ; his capital was Prati-ṣṭhāna
on the Godāvarī).
—शालि-शूक, अस्, m., N. of a
king of the Maurya dynasty (a descendant of Candra-
gupta).
—शालि-होत्र, अस्, m. ‘receiving oblations of
rice or corn,’ a horse; N. of a writer on veterinary
subjects.
—शालिहोत्र-ज्ञ, अस्, आ, अम्, knowing (the
precepts of) Śāli-hotra, skilled in veterinary surgery.
—शालि-होत्रिन्, ई, m. a horse.
—शाल्य्-ओदन, अस्,
अम्, m. n. rice-gruel.

शालीय, अस्, आ, अम्, of or belonging to a hall;
(अस्), m., N. of a Muni.

शालङ्कटङ्कट शालङ्कटङ्कट, अस्, m., N. of
a Rākṣasa (son of Śālaṅkaṭaṅkaṭā, wife of Vidyut-
keśin; the N. is also written Śāla-kaṭaṅkaṭa).

शालङ्कायन शालङ्कायन, अस्, m., N. of a
Muni; of Śiva's attendant Nandin; (आस्), m. pl., N.
of a family (descendants of Viśvā-mitra).
—शालङ्का-
यन-गोत्र, अम्, n. the family of the Śālaṅkāyanas.
—शालङ्कायन-जीवसू, ऊस्, f. epithet of the mother
of Vyāsa.
—शालङ्कायनी-पुत्र, अस्, m., Ved., N.
of a teacher.
शालङ्कायनिन्, इनस्, m. pl., N. of a school.
शालङ्कि, इस्, m., N. of a Muni.
शालञ्च शालञ्च, अस्, m. = शालाञ्चि below.

शालाकिन्, ई, m. a spearman, one armed with a
javelin or dart; a surgeon; a barber.

शालाक्य, अम्, n. a branch of surgery or medicine
(comprising the inquiry into diseases of the head
and its organs; cf. आयुर्-वेद).
—शालाक्य-तन्त्र,
अम्, n., N. of the fourth part of the Aṣṭāṅga-
hṛdaya-saṃhitā (treating of diseases of the head).
शालाञ्चि शालाञ्चि, इस्, f. = शालिञ्च, p. 1003.

शालातुरीय शालातुरीय, अस्, m. (fr. शलातुर),
epithet of Pāṇini.

सालातुरीय सालातुरीय, अस्, m. (for शालातु-
रीय, q. v.), N. of Pāṇini.

शालेय, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, fit for rice (as a field
&c.); sown with rice; (अस्, आ), m. f. a sort of fennel,
Anethum Panmori or Sowa, = मिश्रेया; (अम्), n. a
field of rice.

सालेय सालेय, अस्, m. a sort of fennel or
dill (= शालेय).

शालिञ्च शालिञ्च, अस्, m. the creeper Achy-
ranthes Triandra (the leaves of which are used as a
vegetable).

शालिञ्ची, f. a kind of vegetable (= शौल्फ, appa-
rently somewhat different from the above).

शालु शालु, उस्, m. (according to Uṇādi-s.
1. 5. fr. rt. शॄ, but in some senses connected with
rt. शल्), a kind of astringent substance; a sort of
perfume (commonly called Chor); a frog [cf. शा-
लुर]; (उ), n. the root of the water-lily.
शालुक, अम्, n. (according to Uṇādi-s.

.
fr. rt. शल्), the esculent root of the different kinds
of Nymphæa or water-lily.

शालूक, अस्, m. a frog; the root of the water-lily
(generally neut.); (अम्), n. the root of the water-lily,
(see above); the nutmeg (= जाती-फल).
शालुड, अस्, m., Ved. a frog.
शालुर, अस्, m. a frog.
शालूर, अस्, m. a frog.

सालूर सालूर, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. सल्),
a frog (= शालूर).

शालोत्तरीय शालोत्तरीय, अस्, m. (for शाला-
तुरीय, q. v.?), N. of the grammarian Pāṇini, (this
word is given by Śabda-k. on the authority of the
Trikāṇḍa-śeṣa; it is said to be derived from शाला
+ उत्तरीय, and to account for this derivation a
legend is told that Pāṇini was expelled from the
house of his preceptor for his stupidity, and acquired
his subsequent scholarship by propitiating Śiva.)

शाल्मल शाल्मल, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt.
शल् or शाल्), the silk-cotton tree; the gum or resin
of the cotton tree (= मोच-रस); one of the Dvīpas
or divisions of the continent (= शाल्मलि below).
—शालमल-द्वीप, अस्, m. the Śālmala-dvīpa.

शाल्मलिन्, ई, m., N. of Garuḍa, the bird and
vehicle of Viṣṇu; (इनी), f. the silk-cotton tree.

शाल्वण, अस्, m., N. of a class of herbs (used
medicinally for expelling wind).
शाल्वेय, आस्, m. pl. the inhabitants of Śalva.
षलाग्रु षलाग्रु, N. of a place.

सलिल, अम्, n. [cf. the older form सरिर, p. 1093,
col. 2], water; (in the Sāṅkhya phil.) a technical
term for one of the four kinds of अध्यात्मिका तुष्टि
or internal acquiescence, (the other three being
अम्भस्, ओघ, and वृष्टि; cf. सु-पारा); a kind
of metre; [cf. Gr. σάλος, ἅλς; Lat. salum, sal,
saliva; Slav. sol, ‘salt.’]
—सलिल-कर्मन्, अ, n.
a particular funeral rite (= सलिल-क्रिया).
—सलिल-
कुन्तल, अस्, m. ‘water-hair,’ the aquatic plant Val-
lisneria Octandra.
—सलिल-क्रिया, f. ‘water-rite,’ the
funeral rite of washing a corpse.
—सलिल-ज, अम्,
n. ‘water-born,’ a lotus.
—सलिल-निधि, इस्, m.
‘water-receptacle,’ the ocean.
—सलिल-पूर-वत्,
ind. like a large quantity of water.
—सलिल-रय,
अस्, m. ‘water-flow,’ a current, stream.
—सलिल-
राशि, इस्, m. ‘water-heap,’ any piece of water.
—सलिल-स्थल-चर, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, frequenting
water and land, amphibious.
—सलिलार्थिन् (˚ल-अर्˚),
ई, इनी, इ, wishing for water, thirsty.
—सलिलाशय
(˚ल-आश्˚), अस्, m. a receptacle or reservoir of water,
tank, lake.
—सलिलिले-चर, अस्, आ, अम्, moving about
in the water.
—सलिलेन्धन (˚ल-इन्˚), अस्, m.
‘water-kindling,’ submarine fire.
—सलिले-शय, अस्,
आ, अम्, resting or lying in water.
—सलिलोच्चय
(˚ल-उच्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, having a mass or collection of
water.
—सलिलोपप्लव (˚ल-उप्˚), अस्, m. a flood
of water, inundation.

सलील स-लील, अस्, आ, अम्, playful, wanton,
sportive; (अम्), ind. playfully, sportingly; affec-
tionately.

सलक्षण स-लक्षण, अस्, आ, अम्, having the
same marks, of the same species.

सलक्ष्मन् स-लक्ष्मन्, आ, आ, अ, Ved. having
the same marks or characteristics, related, a relation.

सलज्ज स-लज्ज, अस्, आ, अम्, feeling shame
or modesty, bashful, modest, ashamed; (अम्), ind.
bashfully, modestly.

सललितम् स-ललितम्, ind. with sport,
wantonly.
सलवक स-लवक. See लवक.

सलाजकुसुम स-लाज-कुसुम, अस्, आ, अम्, ac-
companied with sprinkled grain and flowers.

सलेश स-लेश, अस्, आ, अम्, having parts or
portions, with every part, entire; (अम्), ind. with
every particle, entirely, wholly (= 1. स-कलम्).

सलोक स-लोक, अस्, आ, अम्, being in the
same world.
—सलोक-ता, f. the being in the same
world or sphere, residence in the same heaven with
any particular deity (one of the four states into
which Mukti or final beatitude is distinguished).

सल्लकी सल्लकी, f. (= शल्लकी), the gum
olibanum tree, Boswellia Thurifera.
सालकि सालकि, इस्, m., N. of a Muni.

सालन, अस्, m. the resin of the Sāl or Śāl tree;
resin (in general).

सालम्ब सालम्ब (स-आल्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, having
a support or prop, supported.
सालम्बन (स-आल्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, = सालम्ब above.

सालस सालस (स-अल्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, having
languor, languid, languishing.

सालिमञ्जरि सालिमञ्जरि, इस्, m., N. of a
Muni.

सालोक्य सालोक्य, अम्, n. (fr. स-लोक), the
being in the same sphere or world (with another),
residence in the same heaven with any particular
deity (= सलोक-ता, q. v.).
—सालोक्य-ता, f. = सालोक्य
above.

साल्विक साल्विक, अस्, m. (probably a cor-
ruption of सारिका, q. v.), the Sārikā bird.
